newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Smashing Pumpkins drummer pleads to drug charge.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Smashing Pumpkins drummer pleads to drug charge.

text.p: The former drummer for the alternative rock group Smashing Pumpkins, accused of drug possession following the overdose death of another band member, pleaded guilty Tuesday to a lesser charge.
Jimmy Chamberlin was charged with heroin possession after the band's backup keyboard player, Jonathan Melvoin, died of a heroin overdose in New York City July 12.
By agreeing to plead guilty to a lesser charge of disorderly conduct, Chamberlin avoided a sentence of up to a year in jail.
Chamberlin, 32, was given a conditional discharge by Manhattan Criminal Court Judge Donna Recant, provided he successfully completes a drug treatment programme.
If he fails to finish the programme by December, the judge said she would send him to jail for 15 days.
After Melvoin's drug death, the remaining band members fired Chamberlin for what they said was his "insidious disease of drug and alcohol addiction."
